security_audit.summary: The skill is a practical React Native and Expo debugging guide with no evidence of prompt injection, credential theft, or malicious network behavior. Several documented commands are legitimate but risky because they delete caches, reset native tooling, inspect logs, or force-kill processes.

remediation.issue: Destructive cleanup commands are presented without confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to confirm their project path, save work, and review each rm -rf, simulator erase, prebuild clean, and kill command before running it.

remediation.issue: The force-kill command uses command substitution against a port lookup.
remediation.suggestion: Replace kill -9 $(lsof -ti:8081) with a safer two-step workflow that lists the process first and asks for confirmation before termination.

remediation.issue: Log collection commands may expose sensitive device or application data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to redact tokens, user identifiers, and private payloads before sharing Metro, Xcode, or Logcat output.

content.value_statement: Mobile app failures often span Metro, native modules, simulators, and device logs. This skill gives Claude Code and Codex a focused checklist for React Native and Expo debugging.
actual_capabilities: Guides Metro cache reset and packager troubleshooting steps.
Explains native module cleanup for iOS pods, Android Gradle, and Expo prebuilds.
Lists commands for simulator, emulator, Metro, Xcode, and Logcat investigation.
Provides React Native performance checks for slow renders and memory leaks.
Summarizes common error patterns and likely causes for mobile app failures.
limitations: It is a troubleshooting guide, not an automated mobile debugger.
Some commands can delete caches, reset simulators, or terminate local processes.
It does not replace platform documentation for native iOS or Android failures.
It assumes React Native or Expo project structure and tooling are available.

use_cases.title: Fix Metro bundler failures
use_cases.description: Use the cache reset checklist when Metro cannot resolve modules or starts with stale state.

use_cases.title: Investigate native build errors
use_cases.description: Follow iOS pod, Android Gradle, and Expo prebuild steps when native dependencies fail.

use_cases.title: Analyze crashes and slow renders
use_cases.description: Use log commands and performance patterns to narrow crashes, freezes, and render delays.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic debug checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a failing app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to create a safe first-pass checklist for my React Native issue. Ask before suggesting destructive commands.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Metro error
prompt_templates.scenario: Metro cannot resolve a module or starts with stale cache data
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to troubleshoot this Metro bundler error. Explain which cache or dependency checks to try first and why.

prompt_templates.title: Compare iOS and Android failures
prompt_templates.scenario: The bug appears on one platform or behaves differently across platforms
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to compare the iOS and Android debugging paths for this failure. Include the safest log sources to inspect.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a performance investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging for slow renders or memory leaks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to design a React Native performance investigation for slow renders and possible memory leaks. Include evidence to collect before making changes.

output_examples.input: Metro says it cannot resolve a module after I renamed a file.
output_examples.output: A prioritized checklist covering import paths, file casing, dependency installation, Metro cache clearing, and when to restart the packager.

output_examples.input: The Android build fails after adding a native package.
output_examples.output: A native troubleshooting path that checks package compatibility, Gradle clean output, Expo prebuild state, and Android Logcat errors.

output_examples.input: The app freezes when opening a screen with a large list.
output_examples.output: A performance triage plan that checks render time, repeated effects, cleanup functions, and platform-specific logs.

best_practices: Capture the full error, stack trace, platform, and reproduction steps before changing files.
Run destructive cleanup commands only after confirming the project path and saving work.
Redact sensitive values before sharing Metro, Xcode, or Logcat output.
anti_patterns: Do not run every reset command before reading the actual error message.
Do not use force-kill commands without checking which process owns the port.
Do not assume iOS and Android failures have the same root cause.

faq.question: What kinds of projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports React Native and Expo projects that use Metro, native modules, simulators, emulators, and mobile logs.

faq.question: Can it fix bugs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides diagnosis and suggests commands or checks. Code changes still require project-specific investigation.

faq.question: Are the cleanup commands safe?
faq.answer: They are common debugging commands, but some delete caches, dependencies, simulator data, or process state. Review them before running.

faq.question: Does it cover production crash reporting?
faq.answer: It focuses on local debugging and log inspection. Production crash tools may need separate setup and analysis.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatibility.

faq.question: What should I provide when asking for help?
faq.answer: Provide the platform, reproduction steps, full error text, recent changes, package versions, and relevant redacted logs.
